Title: Find a Job

You have to regularly report, to which companies you wrote job applications.
Based on your job applications, new potential job offers are sent to you.

If a job becomes permanent, the process ends, unless you rated the company C or less, then you continue to receive job offers, but no longer have to report.

result.rule: Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.
Use bpmn:sendTask or bpmn:receiveTask when sending or waiting for a message is itself the modeled unit of work.
Use message events for directed participant communication, signal events for broadcasts, and timer events for stated dates, durations or cycles.
Model performer information only when responsibility is stated. Prefer lanes for ordinary organizational responsibility.
Direct each message flow from sender to receiver. Its endpoints must belong to different pools and be valid interaction nodes.
A white-box participant references its process with processRef. A black-box participant has no processRef and no modeled internal workflow.

result.rule: When the description assigns an activity to a role and then describes a dependent continuation of that work without naming a different responsible role: Place the continuation in the same role’s lane unless the description assigns it to another role.

When the description says that a decision must be communicated to an affected participant: Model the communication as a distinct activity on each applicable outcome branch, separate from the decision itself and other branch-specific work.

When the description explicitly identifies the recipient of an activity or output: Include that recipient in the corresponding task label when omitting it would make the task less specific or change its meaning.

When the description identifies the object or information entity acted on by an activity: Label the corresponding BPMN activity using that stated entity rather than substituting a related but distinct one.
